title: Building-Agent: A 3D generation agent framework integrating large language models and graph-based 3D generation model
inputData: 自然语言设计任务 + Rhinoceros场地向量与图结构空间数据
contribution: 提出Building-Agent，将GPT-4的任务理解与决策能力和图神经网络的3D生成能力结合，以图结构表示场地和建筑空间，支持自然语言驱动的3D建筑布局生成、自评估与多轮迭代。
abstract: Building-Agent combines GPT-4 decision making with a graph-based 3D generation model so that natural-language design briefs and site constraints can be converted into graph-structured building-layout decisions and then into 3D voxel layouts.
methodology: Vector site data from Rhinoceros are encoded as graph-structured 3D data whose nodes contain geometric and positional attributes and whose edges encode spatial adjacency. The site graph is serialized for GPT-4 together with the textual design brief. Prompt-engineering modules extract evaluation indicators and compute the Design Requirements Satisfaction Index (DRSI). GPT-4 outputs graph-structured 3D vectors representing building-layout decisions; a pretrained Building-GNN converts those vectors into voxelized 3D layouts. Generated results are evaluated against task indicators, and unsatisfied designs trigger self-iteration while accepted designs are output as 3D models.
results: In Experiment 1, half of the initial layouts had DRSI above 80% and the lowest initial DRSI was 56.25%; after iteration, final DRSI exceeded 90% across tested temperature settings. The best IoU reported was 0.677267 at GPT-4 temperature 0.4–0.6. Experiment 2 evaluated 200 real-world OSM site models; representative scenarios reached DRSI/IoU values including 100%/0.653846, 40%/0.530526, 100%/0.700, and 100%/0.813978. Experiment 3 showed that new natural-language requirements could be added while preserving earlier site/task information, demonstrating memory-supported iterative layout modification.
taskEn: 3D building layout generation and iterative refinement
inputDataEn: Natural-language design tasks plus Rhinoceros site vectors and graph-structured spatial data
operationEvidence: GPT-4 generates graph-structured layout decisions; Building-GNN executes those decisions to create a 3D layout; the workflow quantitatively evaluates generated forms using DRSI and IoU and self-iterates when design requirements are not satisfied.
